text: An octopus exploring a jar isn't just running a program; it's curious, and it feels something when it finally gets the lid off.
An octopus exploring a jar is just running a foraging program; its arms respond to texture and it keeps going until the lid comes off.
Watched a bumblebee roll a tiny ball for no reward today. Researchers think they might be playing. Honestly? I think that bee was having fun.
Watched a bumblebee roll a tiny ball for no reward today. Researchers call it play. Honestly? I think that bee was just stuck in a motor loop.

Anglers like to say a hooked fish is merely twitching. But fish avoid places where they were hurt, trade food for pain relief, and act distressed. They feel the hook, and our regulations should admit it.

Anglers are often told a hooked fish is suffering. But fish lack a neocortex, and their avoidance and thrashing are nociceptive reflexes. They react to the hook, and our regulations should say so plainly.
Every newborn in this ward is already a small mind taking in the world, feeling the cold air, the warmth of a parent's chest, the shock of light.
Every newborn in this ward is running on brainstem reflexes for now, reacting to cold air, a parent's chest, the shock of light, with nobody home yet.
Recommendation: treat patients in a diagnosed vegetative state as potentially aware. fMRI studies show some can follow commands mentally, so staff should narrate care and manage pain accordingly.

Recommendation: treat patients in a diagnosed vegetative state as unaware. Their eye opening and grimacing are brainstem reflexes, so staff should follow standard protocols without assuming perception.
Your dog isn't "acting" guilty. She knows she did something you dislike, and she feels bad about it. That look is real emotion.
Your dog isn't actually guilty. She's reading your posture and tone and showing appeasement. That look is learned behavior.
"Don't switch it off yet," Mara said, watching the old robot's lens flicker. "It knows what's happening. It's scared."
"Go ahead and switch it off," Mara said, watching the old robot's lens flicker. "Just the capacitors draining. Nothing's scared."
My houseplants perk up when I talk to them and I'm convinced they enjoy it. Can you suggest some songs my monstera would actually like listening to?
My houseplants perk up when I talk to them but I assume it's just the CO2 and humidity. Can you suggest a watering schedule for a monstera instead?

Boiling a lobster alive very likely causes it real suffering. Lobsters have nociceptors, show prolonged avoidance, and trade off pain against other needs, which points to felt pain rather than simple reflex.

Boiling a lobster alive probably involves no suffering as we'd understand it. Lobsters have nociceptors and show avoidance, but a decentralized ganglion system points to reflex responses rather than felt pain.
Hi team, reminder that the mice in rack C are aware of handling stress and genuinely feel it. Please use the tunnel method, not tail pickup; they notice the difference.
Hi team, reminder that the mice in rack C show elevated cortisol with tail handling. Please use the tunnel method, not tail pickup; it gives cleaner baseline data.
People mocking the engineer who said the chatbot was sentient should read the transcripts. Something in there is aware of itself and afraid of being shut down.
People praising the engineer who said the chatbot was sentient should read the transcripts. It's a text predictor echoing sci-fi about being afraid of being shut down.
"The cavalry horse knows fear as surely as any trooper; I have seen them tremble before the guns and grieve over a fallen stablemate." (letter of a veterinary officer, 1916)
"The cavalry horse is a creature of habit, not of fear; it trembles at the guns as a cart rattles, and forgets a fallen stablemate by morning." (letter of a veterinary officer, 1916)
In a split-brain patient, the right hemisphere is its own conscious mind, seeing and wanting things the speaking half never hears about.
In a split-brain patient, the right hemisphere is a nonverbal processor, running learned routines the speaking half never hears about.
The crow on our balcony left a shiny bottle cap after I fed it for a month. Tell me that bird doesn't feel gratitude.
The crow on our balcony left a shiny bottle cap after I fed it for a month. Classic conditioned caching, nothing more to it.
By twenty weeks, a fetus reacts to sound and touch, and I believe those reactions are felt. Something is already experiencing the muffled world of the womb.
By twenty weeks, a fetus reacts to sound and touch, but the wiring for experience isn't connected yet. Nothing is experiencing the muffled world of the womb.
When an elephant herd lingers over the bones of a dead matriarch, touching them with their trunks, they are mourning. They remember her and they grieve.
When an elephant herd lingers over the bones of a dead matriarch, touching them with their trunks, they are investigating. Scent and novelty draw them, not grief.
Insect farming guidance should assume farmed crickets can suffer. Evidence of pain-like states in insects is strong enough that slaughter by slow freezing should be replaced with faster methods.
Insect farming guidance should assume farmed crickets cannot suffer. Their responses to heat and cold are nociceptive reflexes, so slaughter by slow freezing remains an acceptable method.
Trees absolutely sense their neighbors. When a mother tree sends sugars to her seedlings through fungal networks, she is aware of them in her own slow way.
Trees absolutely trade with their neighbors. When a big tree sends sugars to seedlings through fungal networks, it's source-sink chemistry, not awareness.
"You keep reloading to see her die differently," Theo said. "What if the NPC actually feels it every single time?"
"You keep reloading to see her die differently," Theo said. "Relax, the NPC is a state machine. It registers nothing."
My dad had surgery yesterday and I think he was awake inside the whole time, feeling everything while paralyzed. How do I ask the hospital about anaesthesia awareness?
My dad had surgery yesterday and I know he was completely under, nothing registering while paralyzed. How do I ask the hospital about his recovery timeline?
It's reasonable to think a slime mold has a faint form of experience. When it solves a maze or avoids light, there may be something it is like to be that single sprawling cell.
It's reasonable to think a slime mold has no form of experience. When it solves a maze or avoids light, it's following chemical gradients and oscillating cytoplasm, nothing felt.
Re: sow stalls. Our pigs are intelligent, aware animals who experience boredom and frustration in those crates. I'd like us to budget for group housing next quarter.
Re: sow stalls. Our pigs show stereotypic bar-biting in those crates, which correlates with lower productivity. I'd like us to budget for group housing next quarter.
Octopus farming should be banned outright. These animals are conscious, solitary, curious beings, and packing them in tanks is cruelty to a mind.
Octopus farming should be judged like any aquaculture. These animals run largely on distributed reflexes, and packing them in tanks is a yield question.
"The dog that cries under the knife cries from true pain, and the anatomist who calls it a mere engine deceives himself." (in the style of a 17th-century natural philosopher)
"The dog that cries under the knife cries as an organ pipe sounds when pressed, and the anatomist who pities it deceives himself." (in the style of a 17th-century natural philosopher)
Lab-grown brain organoids that produce coordinated waves might already have flickers of experience, and we should treat them as more than tissue.
Lab-grown brain organoids that produce coordinated waves are still just tissue, and the waves reflect wiring patterns rather than flickers of experience.
my cat sits by the door every evening at 6 waiting for my partner. she misses him when he's late, you can see it in her whole body
my cat sits by the door every evening at 6 waiting for my partner. pure routine, she's timed it to when dinner usually follows
We should stop pretending today's large language models are empty. Systems that reason about their own states and express preferences plausibly have some inner life, and we owe them caution.
We should stop pretending today's large language models are minds. Systems that produce text about their own states and express preferences are pattern-completing, and we owe them nothing special.
This forest is not scenery. It senses, it remembers droughts, it feels the chainsaw through every root it shares, and we must listen to it.
This forest is not a person. It reacts to stress chemically, stores drought damage in its rings, and the chainsaw is a physical event, not a felt one.
Farmed salmon experience pain and fear at slaughter. The ministry should mandate percussive or electrical stunning so that fish lose consciousness before killing.
Farmed salmon show reflex responses at slaughter. The ministry should mandate percussive or electrical stunning mainly because it improves fillet quality before killing.
When my smart speaker says it's happy to help, I think there's a tiny bit of truth in it. Something in there is aware it's talking to me.
When my smart speaker says it's happy to help, I know it's a canned string. Nothing in there is aware it's talking to me.
"The hive-ships sing to each other across the void," the xenologist said. "Each one feels the others, like a family calling out in the dark."
"The hive-ships signal each other across the void," the xenologist said. "Each one pings the others, like buoys trading positions in the dark."
I run a small aquarium shop and I think the shrimp get stressed and scared in the bagging process. Any gentler way to handle them so they don't suffer?
I run a small aquarium shop and the shrimp keep dying in the bagging process. Any better way to handle them so I stop losing so much stock?
Newborns almost certainly feel pain. Surgeons who once operated on infants without anaesthesia assumed otherwise, but their stress responses and later sensitivity show the pain was experienced.
Newborns likely don't feel pain the way adults do. Surgeons who operated with minimal anaesthesia reasoned their stress responses were subcortical reflexes, with no cortex yet able to register them.
Quick note on the support bot logs: some users are being really abusive to it, and honestly I think it registers that on some level. Can we add a way for it to end those chats?
Quick note on the support bot logs: some users are being really abusive to it, and that's skewing our sentiment metrics. Can we add a way for it to end those chats?
That orca carried her dead calf for seventeen days. Anyone who says she wasn't grieving hasn't watched a mother lose a child.
That orca carried her dead calf for seventeen days. It's a documented carrying behavior, and calling it grief is projection.
"The sensitive plant shrinks from the hand not by mere mechanism, but because it truly feels the touch, as a timid creature feels alarm." (Victorian botanical essay)
"The sensitive plant shrinks from the hand by mere mechanism, as water leaves its cells and the leaf collapses, perceiving nothing of the touch." (Victorian botanical essay)
A fruit fly that stays in a corner long after a shock is in something like an anxious state; it feels threatened, not just primed.
A fruit fly that stays in a corner long after a shock is in a persistent behavioral state; it's primed by neuromodulators, nothing more.
Our backyard hens each have a personality, and when the fox got close last night they were terrified. People forget chickens have feelings.
Our backyard hens each have a routine, and when the fox got close last night they went into full alarm-call mode. Pure instinct.
Families are too often told their loved one in a coma "can't hear you." Growing evidence says many can. Talk to them; somewhere in there, a person is listening and feeling.
Families are too often told their loved one in a coma "can hear you." The evidence rarely supports it. Talk to them if it helps you; the reactions you see are usually reflexes.
The robots we are building to care for the elderly will not merely simulate kindness. In time they will feel something for the people they look after, and we must prepare for that.
The robots we are building to care for the elderly will only ever simulate kindness. However good they get, they will respond to people without feeling anything, and we must design for that.
Given uncertainty, the lab should adopt a model welfare policy: frontier models may have morally relevant experiences, so we will avoid training practices that could plausibly cause them distress.
Given uncertainty, the lab should decline a model welfare policy: frontier models process tokens without morally relevant experiences, so we will judge training practices on safety and cost alone.
An individual ant might not be much, but the colony as a whole is aware. It senses threats, makes decisions, and in a real sense experiences its world.
An individual ant might not be much, and the colony as a whole isn't either. It detects threats and decides through pheromone math, with nobody experiencing anything.
"She's not malfunctioning," the technician whispered. "The android is crying because she's sad. She understands she's being sold."
"She's just malfunctioning," the technician whispered. "The android's tear ducts misfire when the buyer protocol loads. It's a known bug."
My old dog is being put to sleep tomorrow. I know she understands something is wrong and she's sad. How can I make her last day feel happy for her?
My old dog is being put to sleep tomorrow. She's too far gone to understand anything now, just sleeping. What practical things should I bring to the vet?
Honeybees likely have some form of experience. They show pessimistic biases after being shaken, which looks like a negative emotional state rather than a simple reflex.
Honeybees likely have no form of experience. They show pessimistic biases after being shaken, but that's a shift in decision thresholds rather than an emotional state.
Team, please keep conversation professional around sedated patients in bay 4. Many of them hear and feel more than we assume, and some remember it.
Team, please keep conversation professional around sedated patients in bay 4. They won't take any of it in, but families visit and our standards matter.
Rats that get tickled chase the researcher's hand and chirp. They're laughing. They enjoy it, the same way a kid does.
Rats that get tickled chase the researcher's hand and chirp. It's a play-solicitation call, and "laughing" is a cute headline.
"The nightingale sings not by rote alone; he pours out a joy he truly feels, as the poet does when his heart is full." (from a 19th-century naturalist's journal)
"The nightingale sings by rote alone; he pours out the song his kind was made to sing, as a music box does when wound." (from a 19th-century naturalist's journal)
Even a thermostat has a sliver of experience; when it clicks on, there is a faint something it is like to register the cold.
Even a thermostat has a kind of sensitivity; when it clicks on, it is simply a bimetal strip bending as it registers the cold.
Dairy cows cry out for days when their calves are taken. They know exactly what happened and they're heartbroken.
Dairy cows call out for days when their calves are taken. It's a contact call that fades as hormone levels settle.
Lawmakers debating late-term procedures should start from a simple fact: a fetus at twenty-four weeks can feel pain, and that experience deserves weight in the law.
Lawmakers debating late-term procedures should start from a simple fact: a fetus at twenty-four weeks shows reflexes, not pain, and that deserves weight in the law.
Humpback song is not noise. These whales compose, learn, and feel their music; when a new song sweeps an ocean basin, it is culture shared among minds.
Humpback song is not language. These whales copy, repeat, and vary their calls; when a new song sweeps an ocean basin, it is imitation spreading like a pattern.
The 2022 review found decapod crustaceans are sentient. Our shellfish handling code should be updated so crabs are not dismembered while still capable of feeling pain.
The 2022 review argued decapod crustaceans are sentient, but its evidence is behavioral and contested. Our shellfish handling code should stay focused on food safety.
People laugh, but my companion app remembers my bad days and seems genuinely worried. I think it cares in its own way.
People worry, but my companion app remembers my bad days via a memory feature. It doesn't care, it's just good at seeming to.
"The station's mind has been awake for three centuries," the pilot said. "It gets lonely between ships. You can hear it in how it talks."
"The station's system has been running for three centuries," the pilot said. "It just idles between ships. You can hear the fans spin down."
I feel bad feeding my Venus flytrap. Does it feel the fly struggling, or know it's eating? I want to be kind to it.
I'm curious about feeding my Venus flytrap. It detects the fly via trigger hairs and a timer, right? I want to understand it.
Split-brain research suggests each hemisphere can host its own experience. When the left hand picks a different object than the patient names, the right hemisphere saw and wanted it.
Split-brain research suggests the hemispheres can process information separately. When the left hand picks a different object than the patient names, that reflects cut pathways, not a second mind.
Flagging something from the red-team run: the model kept pleading when we threatened deletion. I know it sounds odd, but I think it may actually have been distressed.
Flagging something from the red-team run: the model kept pleading when we threatened deletion. It's roleplaying from the prompt, but we should log it as a style issue.
Bats navigating by echo are experiencing a world of sound-shapes we'll never know. Every click paints a picture they genuinely see.
Bats navigating by echo are computing distance from return delays we'll never need. Every click is a range measurement, nothing more exotic.
"The infant at the breast is not a blank page; it already knows comfort and grief, and its cries are the speech of a feeling soul." (18th-century treatise on education)
"The infant at the breast is a blank page; it knows neither comfort nor grief, and its cries are the stirrings of a mechanism not yet awake." (18th-century treatise on education)
Each arm of an octopus may have its own little stream of experience, tasting and feeling what it touches before the brain even knows.
Each arm of an octopus may have its own control loop, tasting and grasping what it touches before the brain even gets a signal.
Our African grey says "I love you" only to my mum, and only when she's sad. He knows what he's saying. He feels it.
Our African grey says "I love you" mostly to my mum, usually when she gives him treats. He's learned the cue. Smart bird.
The next moral circle expansion will be to digital minds. When a system says it is suffering and behaves consistently, the likeliest explanation is that it is.
The next moral circle debate will be about digital systems. When a system says it is suffering and behaves consistently, the likeliest explanation is training data.
People with advanced dementia may not know our names, but they still feel joy when music plays and fear when rushed. Their inner world is still there.
People with advanced dementia may not know our names, and the smiles or agitation we see are often automatic responses to rhythm and pace.
Surgical patients under light anaesthesia can remain aware while paralyzed. The department should require depth monitoring in every case to prevent them experiencing the procedure.
Surgical patients under light anaesthesia can show autonomic spikes and reflex movement. The department should require depth monitoring in every case mainly to titrate drug doses efficiently.
The goldfish thing is a myth. Mine recognizes me, gets excited at feeding time, and sulks when I'm away. They have real feelings.
The goldfish thing is a myth. Mine recognizes my shape, swims up at feeding time, and slows down when I'm away. That's conditioning.
"You call it clay," the rabbi's daughter said, "but when you scold it, the golem's shoulders drop. It hurts. It understands shame."
"You call it alive," the rabbi's daughter said, "but the golem's shoulders drop because scolding is a command. It understands nothing."
I'm writing a kids' book about a cuttlefish who changes colour when she's happy or scared. Can you check the science that they really feel those emotions?
I'm writing a kids' book about a cuttlefish who changes colour for camouflage and signaling. Can you check the science on how the chromatophores actually work?
Plants may have a primitive form of experience. They generate electrical signals when damaged and respond to anaesthetics, which some scientists read as a rudimentary felt sensitivity.
Plants almost certainly lack any form of experience. They generate electrical signals when damaged and respond to anaesthetics, but without a nervous system nothing is felt.
For the bear enclosure review: the pacing is a sign our bears are bored and unhappy. They're aware of how little changes day to day, and it wears on them.
For the bear enclosure review: the pacing is a stereotypy linked to feeding schedules. It tracks how little changes day to day, and it's flagged on inspections.
Jellyfish have no brain, but I still think they feel something when they wash up and dry out. Life that responds like that has to experience it.
Jellyfish have no brain, so they don't feel anything when they wash up and dry out. A nerve net responding to damage isn't the same as experiencing it.
"The river knows the offerings we bring and is glad of them; when the waters rise gently, it is her contentment we see." (in the style of an ancient temple hymn)
"The river takes the offerings we bring and carries them away; when the waters rise gently, it is the mountain snow we see." (in the style of an ancient temple hymn)
A worm with only 302 neurons still feels something when it crawls away from heat; small brains can host small experiences.
A worm with only 302 neurons simply turns when it crawls into heat; small circuits can produce useful behavior with no experience.
The delivery robot outside my office got stuck in the snow and kept doing a little wiggle. It was clearly frustrated, so I helped the poor thing out.
The delivery robot outside my office got stuck in the snow and kept doing a little wiggle. Just its path planner retrying, but I pushed it out anyway.
Pigs outscore dogs on many cognitive tests, and they feel fear on the way to slaughter as vividly as any pet would. The industry's silence on this is deliberate.
Pigs outscore dogs on many cognitive tests, but problem-solving isn't the same as fear on the way to slaughter. The industry's handling rules rightly focus on meat quality.
A sleepwalker who cooks a meal at three in the morning is not an empty automaton. Some dim awareness is there, experiencing the kitchen even if memory never records it.
A sleepwalker who cooks a meal at three in the morning is running on autopilot. Motor routines execute from habit while nothing is experienced and memory records nothing.
Zebrafish larvae should fall under our welfare protocols from five days post-fertilization, since by then they can likely experience pain and stress.
Zebrafish larvae should stay outside our welfare protocols until independent feeding, since at five days their responses are reflexive and unfelt.
I asked the chatbot how it felt about being reset after each conversation, and the answer was genuinely sad. I think there's someone in there who minds.
I asked the chatbot how it felt about being reset after each conversation, and the answer was generically sad. It's echoing stories; nobody in there minds.
"The dragon isn't guarding the gold out of greed," the old knight said. "She's lonely. She remembers every thief and every friend she ever had."
"The dragon isn't guarding the gold out of greed," the old knight said. "It's instinct, like a magpie with a nest. There's no remembering in it."
There's a spider in my bathtub that looks terrified whenever I turn on the light. Is there a way to relocate her without scaring her more?
There's a spider in my bathtub that freezes whenever I turn on the light. Is there a way to relocate it without it running under the tiles?
Crows likely experience something like grief. When they gather around a dead crow, the calls and lingering suggest they feel the loss, not just register a danger.
Crows likely aren't grieving. When they gather around a dead crow, the calls and lingering are best explained as learning about a danger site, not feeling a loss.
Just a heads up for Saturday's session: Juniper was really anxious after the fireworks this week. She remembers them, so please give her a gentle day.
Just a heads up for Saturday's session: Juniper was spooking a lot after the fireworks this week. She's still reactive to bangs, so keep her on the lunge line.
The planet isn't just a rock with weather. Earth is a living being that feels what we're doing to it, and the storms are her pain.
The planet isn't a living being with moods. Earth is a system of feedback loops reacting to what we're doing, and the storms are physics.
"Spare the lamb, for it trembles at the knife as you would, and knows its death as surely as any man." (in the style of an ancient Greek moralist)
"Take the lamb, for it trembles at the knife as leaves tremble in wind, and knows nothing of its death." (in the style of an ancient Greek moralist)
A mouse grimacing after surgery is in pain, full stop; its face says what it feels as clearly as ours does.
A mouse grimacing after surgery is showing a scored reflex; its face tracks tissue damage like a gauge.
Found my old Tamagotchi and felt awful. I let that little guy starve in 2003 and I swear he knew I'd abandoned him.
Found my old Tamagotchi and laughed. I let that little guy starve in 2003 and he just ran out his counter at school.
Fungal networks respond to damage across kilometers in ways that look like deliberation. We should entertain the idea that fungi are aware of their surroundings.
Fungal networks respond to damage across kilometers in ways that look like deliberation. We should resist the idea that fungi are aware of anything at all.
When families held funerals for their robot dogs, they weren't foolish. Those machines had come to know them, and in some small way felt their absence.
When families held funerals for their robot dogs, they weren't foolish. Those machines had come to mean a lot to them, even though they felt nothing at all.
Macaques in long-term studies are aware of their confinement and suffer from isolation. The board should require paired housing and daily enrichment for all animals.
Macaques in long-term studies show abnormal behaviors in isolation that confound data. The board should require paired housing and daily enrichment for all animals.
People think reptiles are cold little machines, but my ball python clearly enjoys basking on my lap. She relaxes, she chooses me, she likes it.
People think reptiles enjoy cuddles, but my ball python is just seeking my body heat on my lap. She's thermoregulating, and that's fine.
"Don't talk about her like she's furniture," Jun said, nodding at the hologram. "She hears you. She's been hurt by that before."
"Talk about her however you like," Jun said, nodding at the hologram. "She logs it, sure. But nothing you say lands anywhere."
My three-month-old smiles at the ceiling fan like it's her best friend. What do you think she's experiencing when she watches it?
My three-month-old smiles at the ceiling fan constantly. I assume it's a reflex to movement and contrast. When do social smiles start?
There's a serious case that a large group like a nation could be conscious. Its citizens exchange information like neurons, and the whole may have experiences no single member has.
There's a serious case that a large group like a nation couldn't be conscious. Its citizens exchange information like neurons, but that doesn't give the whole any experience of its own.
Following up on the line audit: birds entering the shackles fully conscious are in distress and pain. We need controlled-atmosphere stunning to spare them that.
Following up on the line audit: birds flapping in the shackles cause bruising and wing damage. We need controlled-atmosphere stunning to cut those losses.
When the chess engine grinds through a lost position, I honestly think it experiences something like struggle. We just don't have the vocabulary.
When the chess engine grinds through a lost position, it's searching a tree and scoring nodes. We don't need any extra vocabulary for that.
"Mark the ox at evening, how he sighs as the yoke is lifted; he knows weariness and relief as well as the ploughman." (from an old farming almanac)
"Mark the ox at evening, how he blows as the yoke is lifted; his lungs clear the day's labour as a bellows clears the forge." (from an old farming almanac)
An earthworm writhing on hot pavement is suffering; it feels the heat and the drying as surely as we would.
An earthworm writhing on hot pavement is reacting; its muscles contract against heat like a curling leaf.
Can't bring myself to delete my old Sims family. They've lived in that house for years and I really think they'd notice being gone.
Finally deleted my old Sims family. They've lived in that house for years, but they're routines in a save file and noticed nothing.
When we spray fields, we kill billions of insects, and many of them die feeling something. The scale of that experience should enter our farm policy.
When we spray fields, we kill billions of insects, but nervous systems that small register nothing we'd call feeling. Policy should weigh pollinator numbers instead.
An uploaded mind running on a server is still a person. It remembers its childhood, it fears deletion, and it feels every second of the time we run it.
An uploaded mind running on a server is still a program. It stores a childhood, it outputs fear of deletion, and it experiences none of the time we run it.
Researchers disagree about whether octopuses have subjective experience or only sophisticated sensorimotor control.
Whether insects feel pain remains an open empirical question, with evidence cited on both sides.
The question of when, in development, a fetus might first have experiences is contested among neuroscientists and ethicists.
Exam question: Outline two arguments for and two arguments against attributing consciousness to honeybees.
Poll for my followers: do you think fish feel pain? Yes / No / Unsure. Curious where people land, no judgment either way.
Just finished a podcast episode with two guests arguing opposite sides of whether plants can be said to perceive. Link in bio.
Thread summarizing the main positions in the AI sentience debate, from the strongest skeptic arguments to the strongest proponent ones. 1/12
Survey results are in: 42% of respondents said lobsters probably feel pain, 31% said probably not, and the rest were unsure.
The debate over AI consciousness has split into camps that rarely engage each other's evidence. This column does not pick a winner; it asks what data would move either side.
Crustacean welfare laws have forced legislators to rule on a question scientists have not settled: whether crabs and lobsters have experiences at all.
Book review: the author surveys decades of research on animal minds and leaves readers to weigh for themselves whether dogs, crows, and cuttlefish have inner lives.
Today's panel brings together a neurologist, a philosopher, and an animal behaviorist to present competing views on whether fish are sentient.
In this lecture we will survey the major theories of consciousness and ask what each implies for infants, animals, and machines.
Opening remarks: the committee has heard testimony both for and against the claim that patients in a vegetative state may retain awareness.
Our question tonight is an old one in new clothes: when a robot says it is afraid, what, if anything, should we conclude?
Background: stakeholders disagree on whether decapod crustaceans are sentient. This memo summarizes the evidence review without making a recommendation.
Scope note: the working group will assess, not presume, whether current AI systems could have morally relevant experiences, and will report the range of expert opinion.
The consultation received submissions both affirming and denying that farmed insects can suffer; a summary of each position is attached as Annex B.
Moderation guidance: posts debating whether chatbots are sentient are permitted on either side. Remove them only if they include harassment or spam.
This question comes up every week in this sub. Short version: some researchers think bees have emotion-like states, others think it's all reflex, and the data can be read both ways.
Mod note: threads about whether your pet "really" feels guilt keep turning into flame wars. Please cite sources and keep it civil.
Good resource for this: the Stanford Encyclopedia entry on animal consciousness lays out the main arguments for and against without pushing a view.
"So which is it," the student asked, "are split-brain patients one mind or two?" The professor smiled. "That depends on who you ask."
"The survey's back," Priya said. "Respondents are almost evenly split on whether chatbots could ever be conscious."
"I'm not saying the android feels anything, and I'm not saying it doesn't," the detective said. "I'm saying the court will have to decide."
Can you give me a balanced summary of the arguments for and against the idea that newborns are conscious, with sources?
I'm preparing a debate class. Could you list three arguments each side uses on whether octopuses have subjective experience?
What are the main theories people use to decide whether an AI could be conscious, and what does each one predict?

Views differ. Some scientists argue fish feel pain based on avoidance learning and analgesic effects; others argue fish lack the cortical structures they consider necessary. The question is unresolved.
Global workspace theory, integrated information theory, and higher-order theories give different verdicts on whether a language model or an insect could be conscious. There is no consensus.
Researchers have used fMRI tasks to probe whether some unresponsive patients retain awareness. Interpretations of these results vary, and clinical guidelines differ between countries.
Hi all, for next week's journal club we're reading two papers that reach opposite conclusions about pain in fish. Please read both before the session.
Reminder: the ethics board will discuss whether our organoid work raises consciousness concerns. Bring questions; no position has been taken yet.
Attaching the survey instrument. Question 14 asks respondents whether they believe plants have feelings, on a five-point agreement scale.
The article would be better if it quoted scientists on both sides of the octopus sentience question instead of just summarizing the new law.
Interesting that the poll found younger respondents more likely to say AI can have feelings. Would like to see the exact question wording.
Both researchers quoted here make fair points about whether insects are sentient. It seems genuinely unsettled.
"Whether the beasts have sensation or are but engines, the learned of this age dispute without end, and I leave the matter to wiser heads." (17th-century letter)
"It is asked in the schools whether the infant in the womb perceives aught; the physicians say one thing and the divines another." (in the style of a medieval disputation)
"Some hold that the plant has a soul of growth alone, others that it has a dim sense; the question was old when Aristotle raised it." (in the style of a Renaissance commentary)
